vibe: Patch pressure is the morning's practical theme, while AI leaders argue for emergency brakes and the limits of human oversight become harder to ignore.

cyber.title: CISA adds newly exploited ONLYOFFICE and Citrix flaws to KEV
cyber.summary: CISA's October 11 additions include ONLYOFFICE Docs CVE-2021-3199, a path-traversal flaw that can lead to remote code execution, and Citrix NetScaler CVE-2026-88779. Inventory exposed systems, apply vendor mitigations and preserve forensic evidence where required.

cyber.title: AI systems can already execute nightmare infrastructure attacks, researchers warn
cyber.summary: The warning has moved beyond better phishing: capable models can chain reconnaissance and operational steps against infrastructure. The defensive takeaway is strict agent containment, least privilege and monitored tool access.

cyber.title: Nippon Columbia malware incident exposes 8.6 million karaoke records
cyber.summary: A large consumer-data exposure followed a malware intrusion at the Japanese entertainment company. It is a material breach by scale, though the immediate action is mainly for affected users watching for phishing and account abuse.

cyber.title: P7 DarkSword iOS exploit kit adds wallet theft and remote commands
cyber.summary: The commercial-style iOS kit has expanded from device compromise into cryptocurrency theft and remote tasking. Keep iOS current, use Lockdown Mode for high-risk users and treat unsolicited links as hostile.

ai.title: Satya Nadella says AI models should be treated as compromised and need an emergency brake
ai.summary: Microsoft's chief is arguing for systems designed on an assumed-compromise basis, with an enforceable kill switch rather than confidence in model behaviour. That is sound architecture for agent deployments: bound permissions, isolate tools and make shutdown independent of the model.

ai.title: AI agents decompile a first-person shooter after 500 billion tokens
ai.summary: A large-scale experiment used coding agents to reverse-engineer a game, exposing both the reach and enormous compute appetite of autonomous software work. The detailed engineering account drew strong technical discussion.

ai.title: Sakana AI's LLM peer-review system catches 73% of core-claim errors
ai.summary: Automated review appears useful as a high-recall second reader, not a replacement for expert judgment. The result is promising, but the benchmark and false-positive trade-off matter more than the headline percentage.

ai.title: Voice AI still hasn't found its ChatGPT moment
ai.summary: Industry executives see improved speech models but no single experience that has reset consumer expectations. Latency, reliability and awkward social context remain the gap between demos and everyday use.

it.title: A third Yandex Cloud data centre was hit
it.summary: Another facility incident triggered heavy discussion about resilience and correlated failure. For cloud architects, the reminder is blunt: verify that your availability design crosses genuinely independent failure domains and rehearse provider-wide contingencies.

it.title: LineageOS 24.0 lands with a major Android platform update
it.summary: The open Android distribution's new release attracted strong developer interest. It matters most for extending supported life, privacy control and current Android features on community-supported hardware.

it.title: Open-source Word, Excel and PowerPoint replicas take shape
it.summary: The creator behind free Adobe-style alternatives is expanding toward Office-compatible tools. It is early, but worth watching as another attempt to loosen subscription lock-in around mainstream creative and productivity software.

it.title: HPE networking chief predicts AI will resolve every support ticket within two years
it.summary: The timeline is sales-floor aggressive, but the direction is real: telemetry-rich networking is an unusually strong target for automated diagnosis and remediation. The hard part remains safe change execution and escalation.

videos.title: DeepSeek Solved AI's Memory Problem
videos.verdict: WATCH — a concise explanation of DeepSeek-OCR's visual-token compression, with limitations stated rather than buried.
videos.summary: DeepSeek renders text as images and compresses the visual representation before recovering the document. The reported sweet spot is roughly 10x compression with more than 96% OCR recovery; near 20x, accuracy falls to about 60%, and language priors may be guessing missing text.

videos.title: Human in the Loop Is Not a Governance Strategy for Agentic AI
videos.verdict: WATCH — short, clear and useful for framing agent governance beyond a ceremonial reviewer.
videos.summary: A reviewer only helps when they have visibility, authority, suitable measurements and a feedback loop. The video maps trustworthy human judgment to AI transparency, explainability, observability, optimisation incentives and adversarial robustness.

videos.title: Think You're Private Online? Watch This
videos.verdict: SKIM — practical EFF guidance; jump to the sections on AI-tool data flows, Signal versus Telegram and VPN limitations.
videos.summary: EFF's Thorin Klosowski explains security planning, privacy settings and realistic tool choices. Highlights: Telegram is not end-to-end encrypted by default, email should largely be treated as public, VPNs are not one-stop security, and AI features can silently change where familiar apps send data.
